newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks slump, pare losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks slump, pare losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks fell for the fourth session running Monday but recovered significant ground at the close and could open firm Tuesday if a key U.S. index comes in line with forecasts, dealers said.
"The market put in a good performance considering the Dow was weak and bidding on the local trading floor fizzled," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro. "The mood here remains optimistic."
The blue-chip MerVal index pulled off a low of 652.85 to close at 656.51 with a loss of 0.8 percent. It shows a 4.4 percent drop since last Wednesday.

Floor volume shrank to a dismal 15.5 million pesos from an already weak 23 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals soared to 296.3 million pesos from 135.5 millon Friday. Traders shrugged off the OTC surge as normal end-of-month position squaring.
"Because floor volume shrank so much we may be near support levels," said a technical analyst.
Traders noted smaller MerVal stocks outperformed the heavyweights, underscoring positive sentiment.
"ADRs fell prey to Wall Street but stocks traded only locally fared much better, which is good," said Alessandro.
The bolsa's all-share index closed off 1.2 percent in the session, with losers pounding winners 37 to nine and 14 issues closing flat.
The only main-tier gains were in pulp maker Celulosa, which climbed 1.2 percent, and carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, up 1.0 percent and 0.4 percent each.
Heaviest MerVal losers were Banco Frances and Bansud banks, which pulled back 2.9 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively, and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, down 2.7 percent.
